body_text: Previously announced acquisition by Zymeworks expected to close in second half of 2026 YUPELRI ® Collaboration Revenue increased 11% year-over-year 1, from $18.7 million to $20.7 million, driven by continued Net Sales growth and improved operating leverage Organizational restructuring and cost reduction initiatives delivered 35% reduction in operating expenses year-over-year (excluding restructuring and transaction costs) Q2 2026 TRELEGY net sales, reported by GSK, of approximately $1.0 billion; high confidence in achieving the $100 million 2026 milestone payment 2 Quarter-end cash balance of $388 million and no debt DUBLIN , Aug. 10, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Theravance Biopharma, Inc. ("Theravance Biopharma" or the "Company") (NASDAQ: TBPH) today reported financial and operational results for the second quarter of 2026. "During the second quarter, we entered into a definitive agreement to be acquired by Zymeworks, marking the culmination of a comprehensive strategic review process and what we believe achieves the greatest value for Theravance Biopharma shareholders," said Rick E Winningham, Chief Executive Officer of Theravance Biopharma. "At the same time, YUPELRI ® delivered another strong quarter, underscoring the durability and value of our core commercial asset and the continued execution of our collaboration with Viatris. We continued to execute well against our restructuring plan and expect to close the Zymeworks transaction in the second half of 2026 subject to shareholder approval and customary closing conditions." Pending Acquisition by Zymeworks On June 29, 2026, following a comprehensive strategic alternatives review process conducted by the Company's Strategic Review Committee and Board of Directors, Theravance Biopharma announced that it had entered into a definitive agreement pursuant to which Zymeworks Inc. will acquire the Company for $17.00 per share in cash, plus a contingent value right (CVR) entitling shareholders to 80% of net proceeds realized from any future license, divestiture or other monetization of ampreloxetine over the next ten years. The transaction is expected to close in the second half of 2026, subject to approval by Theravance Biopharma shareholders and satisfaction of other customary closing conditions. Operational Highlights YUPELRI ® (revefenacin) inhalation solution, the first and only once-daily, nebulized LAMA (long-acting muscarinic antagonist) bronchodilator approved in the U.S. for the maintenance treatment of patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD): Quarterly U.S. net sales of $70.7 million, recognized by Viatris, in Q2 2026, increasing 7% year-over-year (YoY) (Q2 2026 vs Q2 2025)1 driven by customer demand growth of 10% YoY (Q2 2026 vs Q2 2025).3 Increased doses pulled through the hospital channel by 25% YoY (Q2 2026 vs Q2 2025), reflecting another excellent quarter of growth.4 TRELEGY GSK reported second quarter 2026 global net sales of approximately $1.0 billion and year-to-date net sales of approximately $1.9 billion5: FY 2025 global net sales of approximately $3.9 billion triggered a $50M milestone payment from Royalty Pharma, with cash received in February 2026. FY 2026 global net sales of ~$3.5 billion required to trigger an additional $100M milestone payment from Royalty Pharma. Organizational Restructuring Update Following the announcement of the Company's Phase 3 CYPRESS results in March 2026, Theravance Biopharma has made substantial progress on its organizational restructuring. As an indicator of this progress, operating expenses (excluding restructuring and transaction costs) decreased 35% year-over-year in Q2 2026 compared to Q2 2025, with additional reductions expected in 2H 2026. The restructuring is expected to reduce operating expenses by approximately 60%, relative to 2025 actuals of $111.1 million. The full run-rate cost savings of approximately $70 million are expected to materialize in the second half of 2026. This is expected to result in approximately $60 - $70 million of annualized cash flow (excluding restructuring and transaction costs), with the benefit expected to be realized beginning in the second half of 2026. Second Quarter Financial Results Revenue: Total revenue for the second quarter of 2026 was $20.7 million, consisting entirely of Viatris collaboration revenue. Viatris collaboration revenue increased by $2.0 million, or 11%, in the second quarter compared to the same period in 2025. The Viatris collaboration revenue represents amounts receivable from Viatris and comprises the Company's 35% share of net sales of YUPELRI, as well as its proportionate amount of the total shared commercial costs incurred by the two companies. The non-shared YUPELRI costs incurred by Theravance Biopharma are recorded within operating expenses. While Viatris records the total net sales of YUPELRI within its financial statements, Theravance Biopharma's implied 35% share of net sales of YUPELRI for the second quarter of 2026 was $24.7 million which represented a 7% increase compared to the same period in 2025. Research and Development (R&D) Expenses: R&D expenses for the second quarter of 2026 were $4.7 million, compared to $10.5 million in the same period in 2025. The reduction was driven by the corporate restructuring announced in March 2026 and the ongoing wind-down of the CYPRESS clinical trial. Second quarter R&D expenses included total non-cash share-based compensation of $0.6 million. Selling, General and Administrative (SG&A) Expenses: SG&A expenses for the second quarter of 2026 were $14.2 million, compared to $18.4 million in the same period in 2025. The reduction was primarily driven by the corporate restructuring announced in March 2026. Second quarter SG&A expenses included total non-cash share-based compensation of $3.6 million. Restructuring Expenses: Restructuring expenses for the second quarter of 2026 were $4.0 million and were comprised of severance costs and termination-related benefits. Cash restructuring expenses were $2.2 million and non-cash restructuring expenses were $1.8 million. Transaction-Related Expenses: Transaction-related expenses associated with the pending acquisition by Zymeworks were $6.1 million in the second quarter of 2026 and were related to legal and financial advisory services. Share-Based Compensation: Total share-based compensation expenses for the second quarter of 2026 were $6.0 million which included restructuring-related share-based compensation expenses. Excluding restructuring-related expenses, share-based compensation was $4.1 million, compared to $4.5 million in the same period in 2025. Share-based compensation expenses for the second quarter of 2026 consisted of $0.6 million for R&D, $3.6 million for SG&A, and $1.8 million related to the restructuring. Net Loss: Net loss was $5.9 million in the second quarter of 2026 compared to net income of $54.8 million in the same period in 2025. The second quarter of 2025 net income was primarily due to a $75.1 million net gain on contingent milestone and royalty assets (representing the sale of our remaining interest in TRELEGY royalties in June 2025). Non-GAAP Net Income (Loss) from Operations 6 : Non-GAAP net income from operations was $9.5 million in the second quarter of 2026 compared to a non-GAAP net loss from operations of $4.2 million in the same period in 2025. See the section titled "Non-GAAP Financial Measures" for more information. Cash Position: Cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities totaled $387.7 million as of June 30, 2026. Shares Outstanding : The Company had 51,890,754 ordinary shares outstanding as of June 30, 2026. Conference Call Earnings results are being released via press release only. The Company will not host a conference call or webcast to discuss quarterly results. title: Datavault AI Reports Second Quarter 2026 Financial Results and Provides Business Update Highlighting Progress Toward Commercialization of Tokenization and Data Monetization Platforms
summary: Datavault AI reiterates its full-year 2026 revenue target of at least $200 million Video demonstrations of the Company’s exchange platforms…...
body_text: Datavault AI Reports Second Quarter 2026 Financial Results and Provides Business Update Highlighting Progress Toward Commercialization of Tokenization and Data Monetization Platforms August 19, 2026 7:44am EDT Related Documents Earnings Webcast Audio NT 10-Q HTML Datavault AI reiterates its full-year 2026 revenue target of at least $200 million Video demonstrations of the Company’s exchange platforms are available online: https://www.dvltinvestor.com/ Q2 2026 Revenue increased 287% compared to Q2 2025 Strengthened leadership with the appointments of cybersecurity veteran Barry Childe as Chief Information Security Officer and Dean Becker as Chief Licensing Officer PHILADELPHIA--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Datavault AI Inc. (“Datavault AI” or the “Company”) (NASDAQ: DVLT), an Artificial Intelligence Platform (“AIP”) company providing data monetization, credentialing, digital engagement, real-world asset (“RWA”) tokenization and spatial audio technologies, today reported financial results for the second quarter ended June 30, 2026, and provided an update on the Company’s strategy to assemble and vertically integrate the infrastructure required to support the commercialization of its data monetization and tokenization platforms. “Over the past few months, we made significant progress assembling the technology, infrastructure and strategic capabilities required to bring Datavault AI’s platform to market at scale,” said Nathaniel Bradley, Chief Executive Officer of Datavault AI. “With the NYIAX acquisition completed and the acquisition of CyberCatch under definitive agreement, the continued buildout of SanQtum and several other commercial programs underway, we believe the foundation of our platform is taking shape. Each component of our integrated technology ecosystem serves a distinct role: NYIAX is expected to provide exchange infrastructure and IP; CLEAR provides identity and credentialing; Fiserv provides payments and settlement capabilities; IBM watsonx is our AI infrastructure; Available powers our distributed edge-computing network, and CyberCatch is expected to strengthen security and compliance.” “These partnerships were never intended to operate independently,” Mr. Bradley continued. “Together, they form an integrated ecosystem. With the core platform buildout well underway, our focus for the second half of 2026 shifts to execution: launching our exchanges, scaling SanQtum and converting our contracted opportunities into commercial activity and recognized revenue.” Business Highlights Completed the acquisition of NYIAX, the Company's fifth owned exchange which adds programmatic, blockchain-based ad-contract infrastructure to the Information Data Exchange® Entered into a definitive agreement to acquire CyberCatch Holdings, Inc., with the proposed acquisition expected to integrate AI-enabled cyber-risk mitigation and quantum-resistant security natively into the SanQtum edge platform Advanced its collaboration with Fiserv to integrate Datavault AI’s patented data monetization and tokenization technologies with Fiserv’s financial technology infrastructure Continued nationwide build-out of its quantum-ready GPU edge network with Available Infrastructure, following the initial New York and Philadelphia deployments Expanded sports and entertainment monetization initiatives through athlete and legacy licensing relationships, including Tyson Fury, Roberto Clemente, Darryl Strawberry and Dwight “Doc” Gooden Entered into an agreement with Perpetuals.com designed to provide international secondary-market access for tokenized RWAs, and advanced its strategic minerals initiative with Patriot Strategic Metals Announced plans to tokenize Available Infrastructure’s Project Qestrel SanQtum Infrastructure Expansion and Project Qestrel During the second quarter, Datavault AI advanced its partnership with Available Infrastructure to build out its SanQtum-powered edge AI infrastructure. SanQtum provides the secure, distributed computing layer supporting Datavault AI's broader platform, combining zero-trust networking, quantum-resilient security, high-performance GPU compute and AI inference at the edge. The Company's initial SanQtum deployments in New York and Philadelphia are the first steps in a much broader planned nationwide network designed to bring secure compute closer to where data is generated, valued, and monetized. On July 17, 2026, advancing this infrastructure strategy, Datavault AI announced the tokenization and monetization of Available Infrastructure’s Project Qestrel, a planned nationwide fleet of 1,000 cybersecure, sovereign edge data centers across 100 U.S. cities and more than 30 states. Each Qestrel site is expected to use Available Infrastructure’s SanQtum technology stack, including zero-trust networking, quantum-resilient encryption, high-performance computing and edge AI inference. Datavault AI intends to use its patented tokenization technology and Information Data Exchange® platform to create $QEST utility tokens representing access and usage rights to compute capacity across the Project Qestrel network. Q2-2026 Consolidated Results Revenue for the three months ended June 30, 2026 was $6.7 million, an increase of $5.0 million, or 287%, from $1.7 million for the three months ended June 30, 2025. Gross profit for the three months ended June 30, 2026 was $2.9 million, compared to $35,000 for the three months ended June 30, 2025. Research and development expenses were $7.2 million, an increase of $3.0 million from $4.2 million for the three months ended June 30, 2025. Sales and marketing expenses were $7.2 million, an increase of $5.5 million from $1.7 million for the three months ended June 30, 2025. title: Ber Months 2026: Why Filipino Christmas Starts on 1 September
summary: September 1 kicks off the world's longest Christmas season. Here's what the Ber Months mean for Filipinos in the U.S.—and what to know about sending money home.
body_text: Quick answer: The “Ber Months” refer to September, October, November, and December—the four months whose names end in “-ber.” For Filipinos around the world, September 1 marks the unofficial start of the Christmas season, a tradition rooted in deep cultural and religious values that turns the Philippines into a nation of decorators, gift-givers, and celebrants for a full four months. If you’ve ever walked into a Filipino household and heard Christmas carols playing in early September , you weren’t imagining things. The moment the calendar flips to September 1, something shifts. Parols—the iconic star-shaped Filipino lanterns—appear in windows. Malls cue the holiday music. Group chats light up with “Ber months na!” And for millions of Filipinos living and working abroad, including across the United States, the countdown to Christmas begins in earnest. The Ber Months are more than a cultural quirk. They represent one of the longest, most heartfelt, and most economically significant holiday traditions in the world. For the Filipino diaspora in the U.S., this four-month stretch carries a particular weight—it’s the season of balikbayan boxes, remittances, and gifts sent across oceans to family back home. Here’s everything you need to know about the Ber Months 2026, why they matter, and what to expect as September 1 approaches. What Are the Ber Months? The Ber Months are simply September, October, November, and December—each sharing the “-ber” suffix in their names. In Filipino culture, these four months collectively mark the Christmas season. While the Western world typically kicks off the holidays in late November (after Thanksgiving), Filipinos start four months earlier. The tradition has no single founder or official proclamation behind it. It evolved organically, shaped by the Philippines’ deep Catholic heritage, colonial Spanish influence, and the Filipino people’s genuine love of celebration. Christmas in the Philippines is a communal, family-centered affair—and four months is barely enough time to prepare for it. By 2026, the Ber Months will look much the same: festive and full of anticipation, both in the Philippines and across Filipino communities worldwide. Why Do Filipinos Start Christmas So Early? The short answer is faith and family. The Philippines is one of the most predominantly Catholic countries in Asia, and Christmas is the most sacred celebration of the year. Preparations—spiritual, social, and practical—take time. There’s also the tradition of Simbang Gabi, a novena of nine evening Masses held from December 16 to 24. Many Filipino families spend months looking forward to this spiritual practice, which brings entire communities together before dawn. Starting the festive spirit in September creates the emotional runway for that kind of devotion. Beyond religion, Christmas in the Philippines is deeply tied to family reunions. For Filipinos living overseas, September 1 triggers a long planning process: booking flights home, organizing gifts, arranging balikbayan boxes, and coordinating with relatives. Starting early isn’t just tradition—it’s practical necessity. What Happens During the Ber Months in 2026? Each month has its own rhythm: September sets the mood. Decorations go up, holiday playlists return, and Filipinos begin budgeting for the season ahead. In malls across Manila—and in Filipino stores across U.S. cities—Christmas displays appear almost overnight. October brings the energy up a notch. Gift shopping begins in earnest, and balikbayan boxes start getting packed and shipped to ensure they arrive on time. November is dominated by preparation. The Feast of All Saints’ Day on November 1 is a major occasion in itself, blending solemnity with family togetherness. By mid-November, Christmas is everywhere. December is the crescendo. Simbang Gabi begins on December 16, and the celebrations run through December 25—and often into the New Year with Epiphany traditions. How the Ber Months Affect Spending and Money Transfers For Filipinos in the United States, the Ber Months trigger a significant uptick in financial activity. Remittances—money sent from the U.S. to family in the Philippines—historically climb from September through December. According to the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP), remittances from overseas Filipino workers (OFWs) tend to peak during the fourth quarter of the year, driven largely by holiday-related spending. This matters for practical planning. If you’re sending money to the Philippines during the Ber Months, here’s what to keep in mind: Plan around Philippine public holidays. Banks in the Philippines observe national public holidays, which can affect processing times for transfers. In 2026, key dates to be aware of include November 1 (All Saints’ Day), November 30 (Bonifacio Day), December 8 (Feast of the Immaculate Conception), December 25 (Christmas Day), and December 30 (Rizal Day). On these days, Philippine banks may be closed or operating on reduced hours, which can delay fund availability for recipients. Send early during peak season. The weeks leading up to Christmas are among the busiest for international money transfers. Processing times can be slightly longer during high-volume periods, so sending money earlier in the season—rather than in the final days before December 25—gives your recipient more time to access funds without stress. Check bank operating hours in advance. If your family member in the Philippines needs to pick up cash or visit a branch, confirming that their local bank will be open before a transaction is always a good habit—especially during the Ber Months, when holidays cluster together. The Ber Months and Filipino Identity Abroad For the roughly 4 million Filipinos living in the United States, the Ber Months are a cultural anchor. They’re a reminder of home—of the smell of bibingka at Simbang Gabi, the glow of parols in the window, and the sound of Filipino Christmas carols drifting from the kitchen. Community centers, Filipino churches, and cultural organizations across the U.S. hold Ber Months events throughout September to December: holiday markets, caroling nights, potlucks, and Simbang Gabi services at local parishes. These gatherings do more than celebrate a season—they preserve a sense of belonging. The act of sending gifts and money home during this period is, for many Filipino-Americans, one of the most meaningful expressions of that connection. It’s not just a financial transaction. It’s participation in a tradition that spans thousands of miles. What Makes the Philippine Christmas Season the World’s Longest? The Philippines is widely recognized as home to the world’s longest Christmas season. The Guinness World Records has acknowledged Filipino Christmas traditions , and cultural observers frequently cite the Ber Months phenomenon as a defining feature of Philippine society. Several factors contribute to this record-breaking length: Strong Catholic tradition : Over 80% of Filipinos identify as Catholic , giving Christmas deep spiritual significance. Government and commercial reinforcement : Philippine law and commercial culture both support the extended season—some government agencies even allow Christmas decorations in public spaces starting in September. Family-first values : Filipino culture places enormous importance on family gatherings, and a four-month window allows overseas Filipinos the time to plan reunions properly. Start Planning for Ber Months 2026 Now September 1, 2026 is closer than it seems. For Filipino families—both in the Philippines and across the U.S.—that date signals the beginning of the most anticipated season of the year. Whether you’re planning to visit family, organize a balikbayan box , or simply join in the spirit from afar, the Ber Months offer four full months to celebrate what matters most: love, family, faith, and community. Start the playlist. Hang the parol. The world’s longest Christmas season is almost here. Frequently Asked Questions What are the Ber Months in 2026? The Ber Months in 2026 are September, October, November, and December. For Filipinos, September 1 marks the informal start of the Christmas season—a tradition rooted in Catholic faith and Filipino family values. Why do Filipinos start celebrating Christmas in September? Filipino Christmas celebrations begin in September because of the country’s strong Catholic heritage, long-standing cultural traditions, and the practical need for overseas Filipinos to plan holiday trips, gifts, and remittances well in advance. The “-ber” months (September through December) have become synonymous with the holiday season in Filipino culture. Are Philippine banks open on Christmas and other Ber Months holidays? Philippine banks are typically closed on major national public holidays, including Christmas Day (December 25), All Saints’ Day (November 1), Bonifacio Day (November 30), Feast of the Immaculate Conception (December 8), and Rizal Day (December 30). If you’re sending money to the Philippines, check the holiday calendar and send funds ahead of these dates to avoid delays in your recipient accessing the money. When is the best time to send money to the Philippines during the Ber Months? The best time to send money to the Philippines during the Ber Months is early in the season—ideally in September or October—before the holiday rush begins. Transfer volumes increase significantly in November and December, which can mean longer processing times. Sending earlier also gives your family more time to plan how they’ll use the funds. What is Simbang Gabi and when does it take place? Simbang Gabi is a traditional Filipino Catholic novena of nine Masses held from December 16 to 24, typically in the early morning or evening. It is one of the most cherished religious traditions in the Philippines and is observed in Filipino communities around the world, including in churches across the United States. Do Filipino communities in the United States celebrate the Ber Months? Yes. Filipino-American communities across the U.S. celebrate the Ber Months through cultural events, holiday markets, Simbang Gabi services at local parishes, and community gatherings. The tradition is a meaningful way for Filipinos abroad to stay connected to their heritage and to family back home.

title: How to Build Your First AI Workstation in 2026
summary: A step-by-step guide to building your first AI workstation on Newegg in 2026, from the all-important GPU and VRAM to the CPU, memory, storage and power.
body_text: Building your first machine for local AI feels intimidating, but it comes down to a handful of good decisions made in the right order. Running large language models, generating images in Stable Diffusion, or rendering 3D scenes on your own hardware means no monthly subscriptions, no usage caps and no sending your data to someone else’s cloud. This guide walks you through a complete, no-compromise AI workstation part by part, in the order that actually matters, and explains why each piece is here. Every price below was checked on Newegg on August 15, 2026. If you remember only one thing, remember this: for AI work, the amount of VRAM on your graphics card is the single most important number in the whole build. Why Build an AI Workstation Cloud AI is convenient, but it adds up. A local workstation runs models offline, keeps your prompts and datasets private, and lets you experiment as much as you like without watching a meter. It also doubles as a serious content-creation machine for video editing, 3D and rendering. The catch is that AI is unlike gaming: instead of raw frame rates, what you need is memory on the GPU. A model has to fit inside your graphics card’s VRAM to run quickly, so a card with more VRAM can load bigger, smarter models. That is why we start with the GPU and build everything else around it. Step 1: The GPU and VRAM (Start Here) 32GB of VRAM is what lets this card load large local models. The graphics card is the heart of an AI workstation, and VRAM is the spec that decides which models you can run. The GIGABYTE GeForce RTX 5090 32GB at $4,699.99 is the top of the consumer stack, and its 32GB of VRAM is the reason it belongs in this build. That headroom lets you run larger local LLMs, generate high-resolution images in Stable Diffusion without running out of memory, and keep NVIDIA’s mature CUDA software ecosystem on your side. If the 5090 is beyond your budget, the principle still holds: buy the most VRAM you can afford before anything else. You can compare every current option in Newegg’s graphics card listings . Step 2: The CPU For AI, the CPU feeds the GPU rather than doing the heavy lifting, but a strong one keeps data flowing and handles the rest of your creative workload. The AMD Ryzen 9 9950X at $549.00 gives you 16 cores and 32 threads, which is plenty for data preprocessing, video encoding and 3D work while the GPU crunches models. You do not need a Threadripper for a single-GPU AI box; a top mainstream chip like this is the smarter, cheaper choice for most first builds. Step 3: The Motherboard A creator-focused board with the PCIe 5.0 and connectivity a workstation wants. Your motherboard determines how much you can expand later. The ASUS ProArt X870E-CREATOR WIFI at $509.99 is built for exactly this kind of machine, with robust power delivery for the Ryzen 9, PCIe 5.0 support for the GPU and SSD, fast networking and generous rear connectivity. The X870E chipset gives you room to add drives and cards as your projects grow. Step 4: Memory System RAM is separate from GPU VRAM, and both matter. While VRAM holds the model, plenty of system memory keeps datasets, browser tabs and creative apps running smoothly alongside it. The Corsair Vengeance RGB 64GB (2×32) DDR5 kit at $879.99 is the right target for AI work; 64GB is comfortable for large datasets and multitasking, where 32GB can feel tight. Running two sticks keeps you in dual-channel mode for full bandwidth. Step 5: Storage AI models and datasets are large, and loading them from a fast drive saves real time. The Samsung 9100 PRO 2TB PCIe 5.0 SSD at $399.99 delivers cutting-edge sequential speeds that shorten model load times and give you 2TB to hold several multi-gigabyte models at once. It slots straight into the ProArt board’s PCIe 5.0 M.2 socket. Step 6: Cooling A hard-working CPU needs to stay cool under sustained load. The Corsair Nautilus 360 RS LCD 360mm liquid cooler at $177.49 keeps the Ryzen 9 9950X in check during long training and rendering sessions, and its large radiator handles the heat that comes with hours of continuous work. The LCD screen is a nice touch for monitoring temperatures at a glance. Step 7: Power Supply The GPU is power-hungry, so do not cut corners here. The MSI MAG A1000GLS 1000W ATX 3.1 at $129.99 delivers 1000 watts and, crucially, the modern ATX 3.1 standard with a native 12V-2×6 connector for the RTX 5090. That means clean, stable power for the whole system with headroom to spare, and no adapter cable clutter. Step 8: The Case Finally, a case that fits everything and breathes well. The Corsair 3500X RS-R ARGB at $79.99 is a superb value, with room for the 360mm radiator, clearance for a large GPU and strong airflow to keep temperatures down. Good airflow matters more in an AI box than in a typical gaming PC because the hardware runs hard for hours at a time. Putting It Together Assemble in a sensible order: mount the CPU, cooler and memory on the motherboard first, install the board and power supply in the case, then add storage, the GPU and cables. Here is the full parts list and what it costs today. Component Product Price GPU GIGABYTE GeForce RTX 5090 32GB $4,699.99 CPU AMD Ryzen 9 9950X $549.00 Motherboard ASUS ProArt X870E-CREATOR WIFI $509.99 Memory Corsair Vengeance RGB 64GB DDR5 $879.99 Storage Samsung 9100 PRO 2TB PCIe 5.0 $399.99 Cooling Corsair Nautilus 360 RS LCD $177.49 Power Supply MSI MAG A1000GLS 1000W $129.99 Case Corsair 3500X RS-R ARGB $79.99 Total $7,426.43 That comes to $7,426.43 for a machine that runs large local models today and has room to grow. The GPU is the biggest line item by far, which is exactly right for AI: spend on VRAM first, and let the rest of the build support it. body_text: New alignment, strategic vision, and executive thought leadership prepare Palitronica for the next phase of market expansion based on paradigm-shifting technical innovations [Waterloo, Ontario, August 17 2026] — Palitronica Inc., the Canadian innovator in physics-based hardware and cybersecurity and quality assurance for safety-critical manufacturing and defense infrastructure, today announced the appointment of a new chief executive officer, along with a bench of experienced leaders, aligned across all functions of the organization. These changes follow milestone growth as the company positions for the next phase of market expansion and technical innovation. Co-founder and current chief executive officer, Sebastian Fischmeister, will transition to a new role as chief strategy officer. In this innovation focused role, Dr. Fischmeister will expand an academic incubation program in related physics and artificial intelligence building blocks while continuing his alliance work across government agencies, defense contractors, and global manufacturing organizations. Matthew Monteyne, pivoting from Palitronica’s chief operating officer, immediately assumes the role of chief executive officer. Mr. Monteyne brings a pedigree of transitional growth from early-stage start-up to strategic exits. He has formerly worked with BlackBerry, RideCo (on-demand transit technology and services), and was instrumental in the acquisition of RapidMind by Intel Corporation (NASDAQ: INTC). Fellow Palitronica incumbent, Eric Ritter, formerly vice president of customer experience and success, will elevate his portfolio to chief operating officer, overseeing customer success, production and deployment operations, and corporate administrative functions. Mr. Ritter brings a wealth of proven operational experience with BlackBerry, Teledyne FLIR (formally Aeryon), and cybersecurity firm, eSentire. Joining Palitronica’s executive team is Mark Sangster, as chief marketing and trust officer, after a year of consulting and advisory work with the organization. Mr. Sangster is a recognized author and thought leader in cybersecurity and industry compliance, as well as strategic marketing, from leadership roles at eSentire and Washington D.C. based cybersecurity firm Adlumin, while shaping regulatory standards and compliance across critical economic and government sectors. Co-founder, Carlos Moreno, remains chief scientist, while Hany Kashif continues his successful tenure as director of engineering, overseeing product development. About Palitronica Palitronica, Inc., is the pioneer of electronics hardware testing assurance solutions that combine deep physics and artificial intelligence to ensure electronic functional robustness, resistance to embedded-silicon cyber threats, and confirmed compliance in zero-time-to-exploit in safety-critical manufacturing, including automotive, aerospace, critical infrastructure, and defense infrastructure. title: Ecommerce Fulfillment Automation: Types + Tips
summary: Learn how to implement ecommerce fulfillment automation workflows so you can eliminate repetitive tasks and scale your business.
body_text: Ecommerce fulfillment automation is the practice of using digital workflows and software to manage tasks like order capture and inventory tracking without manual intervention. Ecommerce businesses that rely on manual processes can limit their operational capacity, expose themselves to human error, and compromise the overall customer experience. On an episode of the Shopify Masters podcast , coffee entrepreneur James Hoffmann says he “could never go back to shipping thousands and thousands of products by hand” and that reliable warehouse integration is essential to scaling business operations. Without automation, brands can struggle to navigate market shifts and seasonal spikes as order volumes outpace the physical limits of manual labor. Keep reading to learn what ecommerce fulfillment automation is, explore the digital and physical automation solutions transforming modern operations, and discover how to deploy native Shopify features to remove repetitive manual tasks from your workflow. What is ecommerce fulfillment automation? Ecommerce fulfillment automation uses software to manage and track processes from the moment a customer completes an online purchase until the physical package is scanned at their doorstep. It replaces tedious, hands-on administrative tasks with programmatic digital triggers, with repeatable workflows that can be scaled as your business grows. No longer the sole domain of giant enterprise corporations, fulfillment automation is accessible to mid-market and scaling brands through cloud-based automation software and ecommerce platform integrations. Automated workflows execute background processes in fractions of a second, which decreases your fulfillment cycle times , or the total duration between a customer clicking Buy and the item leaving your loading dock. Types of ecommerce fulfillment automation Order capture and order processing Inventory management Automated picking, packing, and shipping workflows Tracking, notifications, and returns management Customer service and support Achieving operational efficiency requires breaking down your warehouse pipeline into distinct functional categories. Instead of treating your back end as one huge black box, dividing your operations into modular components allows you to target your automation investments where they will yield the highest returns in speed and resource optimization. Order capture and order processing Automated order processing establishes direct links between your digital storefront and your physical shipping hubs. Advanced software reviews incoming details against custom risk rules, confirms payment capture, and transfers the order data down the line. For example, Shopify Flow is a free ecommerce automation app that uses simple trigger, condition, and action logic to eliminate back-office tasks. You can build customized paths that capture payments on low-risk orders, tag high-value accounts, or alert your logistics team when orders require special handling. Shopify store owners can use Flow to build on pre-built templates configured for automated fraud screening. If an incoming transaction hits a certain threshold of risk, the system automatically triggers a fulfillment hold, pausing the pipeline to protect your bottom line from chargebacks. Save hours on repetitive tasks Shopify Flow’s free templates automate abandoned carts, inventory alerts, customer emails, and order routing. Install the app, pick your workflow, and reclaim hours every week—zero coding required. Install Flow Inventory management Automated inventory management systems help you maintain precise, real-time inventory levels across wholesale paths, retail storefronts, and digital channels. The moment an item sells, software instantly updates stock counts across your entire connected platforms to prevent duplicate sales. These systems can also track historic sales velocity to forecast future market demand and automatically generate purchase orders before your stock hits zero. Divy Ojha, founder of the produce delivery service Odd Bunch, says on Shopify Masters that scaling the brand’s delivery model required depending on systems rather than people. He used Shopify alongside dedicated plug-in apps to automate Odd Bunch’s logistics, ensuring it never overbuys or stores more than it needs. This gives it the organizational ability to fulfill and deliver up to 100,000 orders every week. The Shopify Fulfillment Network allows you to directly integrate your store with premium third-party logistics (3PL) partners like Flexport, ShipBob, and ShipMonk. This software integration enables real-time inventory synchronization across the network, ensuring your online stock availability reflects what’s actually in your warehouse. Automated picking, packing, and shipping workflows Modern fulfillment automation technologies convert incoming data into optimized, digital pick-and-pack instructions. As your operation scales, you can introduce automated physical infrastructure like conveyor networks, smart sorting bins, or automated storage and retrieval machinery to bring products straight to pack stations. Tom Hassell, president of the apparel brand Life Is Good , says on Shopify Masters that implementing robotics and automated workflows into the brand’s fulfillment center has made the environment feel calm and structured, even as the team processes more than 4,000 orders a day. Instead of replacing people, the tech eliminated repetitive physical strain, boosting labor efficiency and allowing workers to pivot to supervisory tasks. Shopify provides an intuitive suite of built-in features , including automated digital pick lists, bulk fulfillment capabilities, flexible fulfillment holds, and intelligent order routing rules to optimize your physical workflows. You can also buy and print shipping labels directly from your admin dashboard, eliminating the need to manually export customer data into external courier portals. Brands selling digital goods or working with fully integrated dropshipping suppliers can use the automatic fulfillment setting to mark orders as fulfilled and send fulfillment parameters to external systems the moment payment is verified. Tracking, notifications, and returns management Consumers expect immediate transparency throughout the shipping window. Automating your post-purchase loop captures tracking data the second a label is printed, instantly triggering delivery updates via email or SMS. This automated communication satisfies customer expectations and reduces inbound support ticket volumes. Additionally, automating the returns process via self-service portals enables customers to print their own return labels, which keeps your global inventory levels updated without requiring administrative labor. Customer service and support Shipping exceptions, transit delays, and address corrections are some common reasons for support tickets. Connecting fulfillment systems to your support platform lets chatbots pull real-time tracking data to answer order status questions. When carrier delays occur, automated workflows tag the affected customer account, update your order management logs, and issue surprise loyalty points or discount codes. This immediate, transparent response converts a negative shipping delay into an opportunity to improve customer satisfaction . Ecommerce fulfillment automation FAQ How does automated ecommerce fulfillment work? Automated fulfillment connects your storefront, inventory management software, and warehouse infrastructure through secure application programming interfaces (APIs). When a customer checks out, automation software evaluates the transaction, updates stock counts across all channels to ensure order accuracy, and routes the order to the nearest fulfillment center. On the floor, this digital data automatically guides staff or automated retrieval systems along the most efficient picking path, generating shipping labels without any manual data entry. What is an example of ecommerce fulfillment automation? An example of ecommerce fulfillment automation comes from Kevin Espiritu, founder of the gardening brand Epic Gardening , who automated his scaling operations by offloading manual fulfillment to a tech-enabled 3PL. On Shopify Masters , Kevin explains that he used Shopify to integrate with ShipStation to fulfill orders, which pass instantly from his storefront to the fulfillment software. This eliminates daily manual work and lowers their overhead. How do you automate ecommerce? Map your current fulfillment process to identify the most time-consuming administrative bottlenecks. Begin by using native tools like Shopify Flow to establish automated fraud screening and order tagging. Next, link your storefront to a warehouse management system or a tech-backed 3PL partner via the Shopify Fulfillment Network to automate label generation and inventory sync.

body_text: View All News Janux Therapeutics Reports Second Quarter 2026 Financial Results and Business Highlights August 6, 2026 JANX007 Phase 1b enrollment continues across taxane-naïve monotherapy and darolutamide combination cohorts JANX014 Phase 1 study continues enrolling patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC) JANX011 Phase 1 healthy volunteer study progressing as planned JANX013 remains on track for clinical initiation in the second half of 2026 Strong balance sheet supports advancement of multiple clinical programs with $970.9 million in cash, cash equivalents and short-term investments at end of 2Q26 SAN DIEGO--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Janux Therapeutics, Inc. (Nasdaq: JANX) (Janux), a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing a broad pipeline of novel immunotherapies, today reported financial results for the quarter ended June 30, 2026, and provided a business update. "During the second quarter we continued to execute across our clinical portfolio while preparing for multiple upcoming milestones," said David Campbell, Ph.D., President and Chief Executive Officer of Janux. "Enrollment continues across our prostate cancer programs, including JANX007 and JANX014, and we remain on track to initiate clinical development of JANX013 later this year. We also continue to make progress with JANX011 in healthy volunteers as we advance our autoimmune disease pipeline." BUSINESS HIGHLIGHTS AND RECENT DEVELOPMENTS: Clinical & Pipeline Progress JANX007 (PSMA-TRACTr) continues to enroll in its Phase 1b trial in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC), with ongoing dose optimization and expansion in taxane-naïve patients. An expansion cohort evaluating JANX007 in combination with darolutamide, an androgen receptor pathway inhibitor, is actively enrolling in taxane-naïve mCRPC. JANX014 (PSMA-TRACTr) , a double-masked tumor-activated T cell engager, continues enrollment in its Phase 1 clinical study designed to evaluate safety, pharmacokinetics and preliminary antitumor activity. JANX011 (CD19-ARM) continues enrolling in its Phase 1 clinical trial in healthy volunteers. The Company continues to advance additional TRACTr, TRACIr and ARM programs for potential future development. Upcoming Milestones Initial clinical data from the Phase 1 healthy volunteer study of JANX011 expected to be announced in the second half of 2026. Clinical initiation of JANX013, a PSMA-targeted CD28 costimulatory TRACIr, expected in the second half of 2026. Additional clinical data for JANX007 expected to be announced at a future medical congress in the first half of 2027. SECOND QUARTER 2026 FINANCIAL RESULTS: Cash and cash equivalents and short-term investments: As of June 30, 2026, Janux reported cash and cash equivalents and short-term investments of $970.9 million, compared to $966.6 million on December 31, 2025. Research and development expenses: Research and development expenses were $31.0 million for the quarter ended June 30, 2026, compared to $34.7 million for the comparable period in 2025. General and administrative expenses: General and administrative expenses were $11.0 million for the quarter ended June 30, 2026, compared to $10.5 million for the comparable period in 2025. Net loss: Net loss was $22.0 million for the quarter ended June 30, 2026, compared to $33.9 million for the comparable period in 2025. About Janux Therapeutics Janux is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing a broad pipeline of novel immunotherapies by applying its proprietary technology to its Tumor Activated T Cell Engager (TRACTr), Tumor Activated Immunomodulator (TRACIr), and Adaptive Immune Response Modulator (ARM) platforms. Janux’s lead clinical candidate, JANX007, is a PSMA-targeted TRACTr being investigated in a Phase 1 clinical trial in patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC). The Company is also advancing additional PSMA-targeted programs, including JANX014, a double-masked PSMA TRACTr being evaluated in a Phase 1 clinical trial, and JANX013, a CD28 co-stimulatory TRACIr designed for combination with JANX007. Beyond its prostate cancer programs, Janux’s pipeline includes JANX011, a CD19-targeted ARM being evaluated in a Phase 1 clinical trial in healthy adult volunteers for potential treatment of autoimmune diseases. Janux continues to generate additional TRACTr, TRACIr, and ARM programs for potential future development. For more information, please visit www.januxrx.com and follow us on LinkedIn.
